name: @sure/client
//typescript: Capped at 5.x by `openapi-typescript`, which peers `typescript: ^5.x`. That is the whole workspace's ceiling, so all three packages move together. Re-measured 2026-10-30: openapi-typescript 7.13.0 is still the newest release and still peers `^5.x`. Stable 6.0.3 (still the newest 6.x) builds clean: gen:client is byte-identical, and the web and api-tests typechecks pass. But it leaves openapi-typescript as the tree's only unmet peer (`pnpm peers check` is otherwise silent) for no measured gain, so it is not worth taking ahead of upstream. npm `latest` is 7.x and is blocked outright; see the note in packages/web.
//openapi-fetch: 0.17's `Readable<T>` (openapi-typescript-helpers 0.1.0) still collapses tuples: a Rust `Vec<(A, B)>` in a response generates `[A, B][]` but reads back as `(A | B)[][]`. Upstream fixes openapi-ts/openapi-typescript#2673 and #2842 are both still open (2026-10-30). The cap below 0.17 was lifted on 2026-10-30 because no response type carries a tuple any more: the only one, `StoredTaxScale.brackets`, went in 2e73f09, and web + api-tests typecheck clean on 0.17.0. If a tuple returns to the API, give it a named struct rather than pinning this back. Keep packages/api-tests on the same range so the tree holds one copy.
